# Hub v2 V5: the cache strip, the Tokens page fix, the reading history

Step 5 of 7 of Hub v2. Needs V1. Read PROJECT-BRIEF.md first, then the head comments of `hub/watcher.js` and `hub/runner.js`. No model call anywhere in this step's code (the existing usage probe stays behind its own button). Hub files only.

## Goal
The chat and each run's page show how big the conversation is, whether the cache is warm, and how the last message split into re-used and newly written tokens, and warn before a costly action. The Tokens page is built fresh on every visit, every reading carries a token total so the hub can learn what a million tokens costs, and a reading history is shown.

## Build
1. `hub/runner.js`: the reducer keeps, per assistant message (counted once per message id), `{input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite}` from `usage` (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`) and adds them to the `tokens` feed event. Numbers only. From the `result` event keep the context window size when the summary carries one for the model; when it does not, keep null. The billable count (`input + output + cacheWrite`) does not change.
2. `hub/cache.js` (pure, tested): `contextOf(u) = input + cacheRead + cacheWrite`; `splitOf(u)`; `observe(prev, cur)` returns `{gapMs, hit}` where hit means `cur.cacheRead >= 0.5 * contextOf(prev)`; `lifetime(observations)` returns `{longestHitMs, shortestMissMs, sure}` with `sure` true only when at least 3 hits and 1 miss agree and a model switch was not the cause of the miss; `stateOf({lastReplyAt, now, lifetime})` returns warm, probably cold, or unknown, and a countdown only when `sure`; `rewriteCost(context)` for warnings. Observations are appended to `.hub/cache.jsonl` (gap, hit, model, context; no text).
3. `hub/chat.js` and `hub/runs.js`: store the last message's numbers and the reply time on the chat record and the run record; expose them in `view()` and the run view.
4. Cache strip in `hub/web/chat.js` and the run page: "Conversation size" bar (count, and "of N" only when the window is known); "Cache warm · last reply 4 min ago" or "Cache probably cold" or just the minutes while the lifetime is not sure; a two-part bar "re-used from cache (cheap)" and "written new" with both counts. Warnings: on choosing another model, "Switching model sends the whole conversation again: about N tokens written new" with "New chat on that model", "Switch anyway", "Stay"; on Send when the cache is probably cold and the conversation is over 40,000 tokens, a note with "Send anyway" and "New chat"; a quiet hint to start a new chat above 60% of a known window. The existing second yes for Opus and Fable stays as it is.
5. Token totals: wherever a reading is appended for a chat turn or a run (`appendReading` in `hub/chat.js` and `hub/runs.js`), add `tokensTotal` from the same log scan the watcher command uses (`scanLogs`), taken when the reading arrives, so `learnRate` gets pairs it can use. Do not change `learnRate`'s rule.
6. Tokens: `/tokens` is rendered on every request from the readings (`hub/page.js`), no longer served from `.hub/watcher.html`; `npm run watcher` still writes its file. In the shell, `#tokens` shows both gauges with reset times, the learned rate or "not known yet" with the reason, the reading history (last 30: when, from, this week, these 5 hours, tokens so far) and "Take a fresh reading (one small Haiku call, about 7,600 tokens)", which calls the existing probe with the hub token; pressing it is the owner's go-ahead.
7. Tests: `tests/hub-cache.mjs` (context and split, hit and miss, lifetime not sure with too little data, model switch ignored, warnings) plus updates: the reducer's new fields with the fake CLI (add cache numbers to its scenarios), `/tokens` reflects a reading appended a moment before, a chat reading carries `tokensTotal`. Add screenshots of the chat with the strip and of Tokens to `scripts/hub-shots.mjs`.

## Rules
- Never show a countdown the data does not support. Never print model text into the feed, the strip or the files.
- No BOM. Run `npm test` after each change; finish with `npm run index`, then `npm test`. Stop with tests passing; report failures honestly, and say which numbers were only seen with the fake CLI. Do not commit.

## Done when
The strip shows real numbers from the usage each reply carries, the warnings appear before a model switch and a cold send, `/tokens` is always current, new readings carry a token total, and the history is visible.
